summary: Reviewed-source repair candidate for #5273, not installed/native adoption. Preserve the additive versioned hardness/category contract, revision-bound current assessments, immutable original calibration features and separately labelled launch-confirmed versus provider-observed execution facts. Independent source review found that role-prefixed Unknown or partial execution cohorts could erase known card summaries, loose evidence URLs could point at another issue, and shared threads could cross-attribute provider models. The repair uses a JSON string-array summary wire so punctuation in model names cannot become invented role/value separators; native replacement requires every previously known role/value fact, with Unknown-role refinement and same-value confidence upgrades allowed. Different launch and provider-resolved values are both retained. The typed writer binds provenance to the exact selected owning issue and positive numeric comment ID. Shared threads across distinct invocation identities or roles refuse before provider joins. Actual Python projector-to-native migration fixtures cover these controls; hashes establish canonical payload identity while the operating owner still verifies evidence authority. The maintained migration retains its fixed field allowlist, native preimages, source/artifact joins, shared writer lock, possible-send custody, item-scoped groups and final retention checks. Existing binding/enrollment, views and timers remain preserved; publication, actual installed caller qualification, native card/visible-field adoption and refreshed complete metadata backfill remain separate held effects.
title: Additive LEARN card annotations and revision-bound evidence
